claims.claim: Matched Gaussian relative entropy obeys a convex-order reverse triangle inequality for compactly supported laws in every finite dimension.
An L2 spectral gap on S2 implies F_m(T)<=2 exp(-c T/m), and the sharp joint-spectral-radius defect is Theta(1/m).
The five specified rational Bloch rotations satisfy SG.

claims.claim: In the specified clock/deadline-dependent-readout model, finite-gate qubit simulation has Theta(T) state complexity uniformly for 0<=epsilon<=1/72, with an exact O(T)-state upper bound.
Unbiased positive interpolation on arbitrary m-point time-varying grids requires max numerical range expansion at least (1/2) exp(c T/m); an exp(16T/m) upper construction exists for m>=16.
For a finite orthogonal alphabet with identity and all positive weights, rho_m=1 iff a nonzero unit-vector group orbit of size at most m exists.
Finite Gaussian likelihood probes at all scales characterize convex order of compactly supported laws; the raw KL scale profile alone does not.
claims.status: written_derivation; computational advantage and historical novelty unestablished
